content_voiceover: This table drills into the newer structurally-defined B-ALL subtypes, and the annotated summary on the right is the fastest way to learn it: DUX4 rearrangement, NUTM1 rearrangement, and PAX5 P80R mutation are favorable, while MYC rearrangement, MEF2D rearrangement, HLF rearrangement, and CDX2/UBTF are poor risk. DUX4-rearranged B-ALL is actually excellent prognosis despite looking aggressive, it's more common in adolescents and young adults, shows CD371 and CD2 positivity, and often has associated ERG and IKZF1 deletions. MEF2D-rearranged disease, by contrast, is CD10-negative or dim with CD38 and cytoplasmic mu positivity, and carries a poor prognosis. HLF-rearranged B-ALL is very rare but very poor prognosis, though it may respond to anti-CD19 therapy. ZNF384 or ZNF362 rearranged disease is notable for aberrant myeloid antigen expression and overlaps significantly with B-myeloid mixed phenotype acute leukemia. NUTM1-rearranged ALL is enriched in infants who lack KMT2A rearrangements and, unlike most infant ALL, actually carries a good prognosis.
keypoints: Favorable structural subtypes: DUX4-r, NUTM1-r, PAX5 P80R
Poor structural subtypes: MYC-r, MEF2D-r, HLF-r, CDX2/UBTF
DUX4-r: CD371+/CD2+, excellent prognosis despite aggressive look
NUTM1-r: infant ALL without KMT2A rearrangement, good prognosis
keypoint_voiceover: Memorize this favorable-versus-poor split: DUX4, NUTM1, and PAX5 P80R are favorable, while MYC, MEF2D, HLF, and CDX2/UBTF are poor. The classic trap is DUX4-rearranged ALL, it can look alarming but actually carries an excellent prognosis, so don't confuse it with the genuinely high-risk MYC or HLF rearranged subtypes.
